newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to set Thomson-CSF sale terms soon.
newsitem.headline: France to set Thomson-CSF sale terms soon.

text.p: The French government will decide in the next few days on terms for the proposed sale of its 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, including whether to sell it through a private placement or a public offering.
Official sources said on Wednesday that "the government will announce in the next few days the terms of the privatisation of Thomson-CSF."

The sources added that the constitutional court, the Conseil d'Etat, would announce on Friday whether the government should follow the 1986 privatisation law for the sale or a 1991 law which would speed up the sale.

The government has decided to sell the stake in Thomson-CSF as soon as possible, probably early 1997, while delaying the sale of a 100 percent stake in consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
The government on December 4 suspended the planned privatisation sale of Thomson SA -- the company which owns the 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF as well as all of TMM -- to Lagardere Groupe.
It did so after the independent Privatisation Commission had objected against the terms of the planned sale of TMM by Lagardere to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
Lagardere planned to bid for the 42 percent of Thomson-CSF listed on the Paris Bourse and merge the company with its own Matra Defense Espace unit.

Noel Forgeard, chairman of the Matra unit which has a missile joint venture with British Aerospace Plc, told Les Echos newspaper on Wednesday that he was against a public sale of the Thomson-CSF stake.

Thomson has declined comment on newspaper reports that its management, led by chairman Marcel Roulet, prefers a public sale on the share market over a private placement with another company -- Lagardere, Alcatel Alsthom or any another.
"What some are recommending, floating the stake owned by the state in Thomson-CSF, would not expand but freeze the industrial boundaries of Thomson," Forgeard said.
He warned that with a float there could be a core group of different shareholders whose differing agendas could lead to the break-up of Thomson-CSF.
In Brussels, the European Commission said it had opened a formal probe into the planned recapitalisation of Thomson Multimedia.
It said the French government had requested clearance for its plan to inject 11 billion francs ($2.09 billion) into Thomson SA and its debt-laden multimedia division.
The statement did not give details on the injection shareout, but Commission sources said that TMM would get the bulk of it.
